steps.title: Prepare complete culture media
steps.instruction: Make A375 complete DMEM HG medium by mixing 445 mL DMEM HG, 50 mL heat‑inactivated FBS (56 °C 30 min, store aliquots at –25 °C), and 5 mL Pen‑Strep (100 U/mL penicillin, 100 µg/mL streptomycin) to a final volume of 500 mL. Make NHEM complete MBM‑4 medium by adding 9 mL MGM‑4 Single Quots to 500 mL MBM‑4 basal medium (use within one month, do not refreeze).

steps.title: Prime SlideFlasks before seeding
steps.instruction: One day before the experiment, add 1 mL A375 medium and 1 mL NHEM medium to each SlideFlask that will be irradiated or kept as control. Incubate 30 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in a humidified incubator.

steps.title: Detach and count A375 melanoma cells
steps.instruction: A. Aspirate medium from the T‑75 flask, wash with 10 mL DPBS, add 1 mL 0.05 % Trypsin‑EDTA and incubate 5 min at 37 °C. Stop with 4 mL complete A375 medium, pipette up/down three times, transfer 6 mL to a 15 mL tube, centrifuge 200–300 × g (1 200–1 500 rpm) 5 min RT, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 2 mL medium, mix three times, take 500 µL, mix 1:2–1:10 with 0.4 % Trypan Blue, count in a Marienfeld chamber, and calculate that 840 000 cells per 1 mL are needed per SlideFlask.

steps.title: Detach and count NHEM melanocytes
steps.instruction: A. Aspirate medium from the T‑25 flask, rinse gently with 5 mL DPBS, aspirate, add 1 mL 0.025 % Trypsin‑EDTA mixed with 1 mL 0.02 % Versene, incubate 1 min at 37 °C. Neutralize with 2 mL Trypsin Neutralizing Solution (TNS) at RT, wash with 2 mL complete NHEM medium, collect cells, centrifuge 100 × g 3 min RT, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL medium, mix with 0.4 % Trypan Blue, count, and use 420 000 cells per 1 mL for each SlideFlask. Handle gently because NHEM cells detach easily.

steps.title: Seed co‑culture in SlideFlasks
steps.instruction: Add the calculated volumes of A375 and NHEM suspensions to each SlideFlask so that the final density is ~80 %–90 % confluency the next day. Include a separate coverslip for the secondary‑only negative control.

steps.title: Prepare SlideFlasks for irradiation
steps.instruction: Fill each SlideFlask with complete medium, screw caps tightly (add parafilm if vented caps are used) to avoid drying and contamination.

steps.title: Irradiate samples
steps.instruction: A. X‑ray pulsed irradiation: mount SlideFlasks vertically with double‑adhesive tape, operate X‑ray source at 200 kV, 100 µA, 0.2 mm Cu filter, chopper at 19 V, 1.4 kHz, place sample 10 cm from source, irradiate 15 min 31 s (≈2.4 Gy measured with Gafchromic EBT3 films). Use Pb collimators (~4 mm aperture, 0.8 cm thickness) to reduce scatter. B. LPA electron (VHEE) irradiation: deliver electrons from a petawatt laser‑driven accelerator through a 99 % He/1 % N₂ gas jet; monitor dose with ionization chamber, TLDs or Gafchromic films (≈150 mGy in our setup).

steps.title: Post‑irradiation recovery
steps.instruction: Incubate flasks for 30 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to allow γ‑H2AX phosphorylation. If caps are not vented, release slowly; remove excess medium to avoid overflow while keeping cells covered.

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Aspirate medium, wash once with a generous volume of DPBS (≥culture volume) at RT. Fix with 4 % PFA (prepared as described) for 30 min at RT, covering the monolayer. Aspirate PFA, wash twice with DPBS (use at least twice the PFA volume). Fixed cells can be stored in DPBS at 4 °C for 1–2 weeks (preferably process sooner).

steps.title: Permeabilize and block
steps.instruction: Add 0.2 % Triton X‑100 permeabilization solution (3 mL per SlideFlask, 350 µL per coverslip), incubate 3 min RT. Wash twice with DPBS. Add 0.5 % BSA blocking solution (same volume as permeabilization) and incubate 1 h RT.

steps.title: Detach SlideFlasks from slides
steps.instruction: Use the chamber detachment tool supplied with the SlideFlasks to separate the glass slide from the culture chamber.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Add primary antibody solution (mouse anti‑p‑γ‑H2AX diluted 1:200 in 0.5 % BSA) – 350 µL per slide, 250 µL per coverslip. Place slides face‑up in a humid chamber (wet napkins at bottom, lid on) and incubate 30 min at RT. Include a secondary‑only control where only blocking buffer is added.

steps.title: Wash after primary antibody
steps.instruction: Rinse three times with DPBS, 5 min each wash.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Add Alexa Fluor 594 donkey anti‑mouse secondary antibody diluted 1:400 in 0.5 % BSA – 350 µL per slide, 250 µL per coverslip. Incubate 20 min RT in the same humid chamber, protected from light (cover box with aluminum foil).

steps.title: Hoechst nuclear staining
steps.instruction: Incubate with Hoechst 33342 staining solution (1 µL of 10 mg/mL stock per 1 mL 1× PBS, i.e., 1:3 000) for 1 min RT. Wash three times with DPBS and once with MilliQ water to avoid salt crystals.

steps.title: Mount samples
steps.instruction: Apply FluorSave mounting reagent – 100 µL per slide, 15 µL per coverslip – and place the coverslip (for CS samples) centered on the microscope slide. Seal if desired with transparent nail polish. Store mounted slides in the dark at 4 °C for up to 1 month (preferably image sooner).

steps.title: Set up microscope and acquire images
steps.instruction: Power on microscope, lamp, and computer. Install slide holder, calibrate motorized stage. Place slides with cell‑covered surface toward objective. Focus first with low magnification using DAPI channel, then verify TxRed (p‑γ‑H2AX) signal. Set exposure ≤300 ms per channel using negative and bright controls (secondary‑only and cisplatin‑treated samples). Define ROIs (preview at 5×, acquire at 63× oil). Save project in a dedicated folder, keep all acquisition parameters identical for all samples. Acquire images (≥500 cells per sample) and store as grayscale .aqproj files; export as .tiff/.jpeg if needed.

steps.title: Analyze images with TissueQuest
steps.instruction: Open TissueQuest, import the .aqproj project. Select slides and regions to analyze. In ‘Choose Markers’, keep DAPI and TxRed (named Texa), add a virtual marker ‘Texa_DOTS_ON_DAPI’. Set segmentation parameters: nuclei size = 40 a.u., DAPI threshold = 12–80, TxRed background threshold = 5. Choose ‘Various Shapes 2.0’, select events entirely in ROI. In ‘Measured Parameters’, include DAPI Area, DAPI Mean Intensity, DAPI Compactness, DAPI Eccentricity, Texa Mean Intensity, and Dots count on Texa_DOTS_ON_DAPI. Create scattergrams/histograms, set cut‑offs using forward/backward gating (e.g., gate single cells on DAPI Area vs Mean Intensity, then compact nuclei, then eccentricity for cell‑type discrimination). Run analysis on the positive‑control region to fine‑tune thresholds, then apply the same settings to all regions (use ‘Apply Diagram Set to All Samples and their Regions’). Batch‑process all regions, export results, and adjust gates if needed.
